title: When the Portrait Burns
premise: Marguerite Thackeray, a nonbinary property surveyor who trusts measurements more than memories, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House in the drowned valley of Ashen Fen. The house appraises back—rooms appear on their blueprints that don't exist, and the childhood imaginary friend, Wren, is waiting on the porch exactly as they left them twenty-five years ago. Marguerite learns the house keeps the town's erased and forgotten, and that a children's song sung by the vanished holds the only way out—but singing it wrong means joining them. To finish the song's last verse, Marguerite must uncover what the town did to the family who built Hollowmere and choose between belonging to the living or the lost; in the end they burn the portrait at the house's heart, freeing the dead but losing Wren forever, and walk out carrying the last verse as testimony.
about_author: Rafael Marchetti is the pen name of a former building inspector from coastal New England whose reports kept flagging houses that shouldn't have been standing. They now write horror full-time, insisting the strangest things they ever saw were all perfectly up to code.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Grief
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine appraisal of a condemned farmhouse goes wrong when their laser measure returns impossible numbers and the client file lists Marguerite themselves as a prior occupant. Emotional beat: unease dressed up as professionalism.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Marguerite arrives at Ashen Fen to survey the estate, finding a town that floods on maps but not in memory. The locals are polite in the way people are polite around an open grave. Beat: creeping isolation.

chapters.title: Someone on the Porch
chapters.summary: At dusk, Wren—the imaginary friend Marguerite invented at seven—is waiting, unchanged, holding a lantern. Marguerite's carefully built adult identity cracks against a child's certainty. Beat: terror braided with longing.

chapters.title: Rooms That Aren't on the Plans
chapters.summary: Marguerite surveys the interior; corridors extend past the exterior walls, and a nursery exists where blueprints show solid brick. Wren follows, humming a tune Marguerite almost knows. Beat: reality losing its load-bearing walls.

chapters.title: The Song Everyone Half-Remembers
chapters.summary: In town, an old barkeep, Delia, goes pale when Marguerite hums three notes. She warns: everyone knows the first verses, nobody sings the last. Beat: first confirmation this is communal, not personal.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Erasures
chapters.summary: Marguerite digs through county archives: the Merrick family, builders of Hollowmere, expunged from every record after 1931. Their POV tightens into obsession. Beat: justice begins as paperwork.

chapters.title: Wren's Rules
chapters.summary: Wren explains the house's terms: keep the lights on, count the doors, never sing along. Marguerite realizes the rules were the game they invented as a child—and the child knew something real. Beat: dread reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Portrait at the Heart
chapters.summary: Behind a bricked hearth, Marguerite finds a massive family portrait—faces scorched away except one, which watches them. The room is warm like held breath. Beat: the antagonist reveals itself.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Wrong
chapters.summary: Night two: Marguerite counts eleven doors; there were ten. Behind the eleventh, someone sings the fourth verse in a voice like their mother's. Beat: the house starts negotiating.

chapters.title: Delia's Confession
chapters.summary: Delia admits the town burned the Merricks out in '31 over land and lies, then sang the song to forget them—and forgetting became feeding. Beat: guilt of a whole community, justice deferred for a century.

chapters.title: What the House Keeps
chapters.summary: Marguerite enters the east wing and finds the vanished townsfolk preserved mid-life, content and hollow-eyed, including a surveyor who came before them. Beat: horror of comfortable erasure.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't Written
chapters.summary: Research shows the song was a Merrick lullaby; the last verse existed only in the youngest daughter's memory. Marguerite realizes Wren might be that daughter—or made from her. Beat: identity theme sharpens.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Appraised
chapters.summary: The house turns its attention fully on Marguerite, showing them rooms built from their own suppressed memories: a childhood eviction, a name they buried. Beat: the surveyor becomes the surveyed.

chapters.title: Offer of Belonging
chapters.summary: The portrait speaks with the assembled voices of the kept, offering Marguerite a place—valued, remembered, home—if they bring the town's living descendants to sing. Beat: temptation framed as acceptance.

chapters.title: Refusal and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Marguerite refuses and the house retaliates: doors multiply, lights fail, Wren is taken as collateral. Alone, Marguerite chooses to fight rather than flee. Beat: resolve forged from rejection.

chapters.title: The Descendants
chapters.summary: Marguerite gathers Delia and two other old families' heirs, forcing the town to look at what its comfort cost. Some refuse; one young man, Theo, joins. Beat: justice requires witnesses.

chapters.title: Into the Kept Rooms
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Theo enter the house deliberately, using the counting rules as a map to reach the nursery where Wren is held. Beat: courage as navigation.

chapters.title: Wren's True Name
chapters.summary: In the nursery, Marguerite learns Wren is Edith Merrick's imagined companion, given form by the house—a ghost of a ghost. Wren remembers the last verse but cannot speak it without the portrait burning. Beat: heartbreaking revelation.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Marguerite reaches the portrait, and the house throws every kept soul and false door at them. Theo sings the known verses as a shield while Marguerite climbs toward the hearth. Beat: full-throttle escalation.

chapters.title: When the Portrait Burns
chapters.summary: Marguerite sets the portrait alight with the appraisal ledger—the town's own record of theft—as kindling. The house screams itself straight, the kept dissolve into released light, and the last verse finally sounds, sung by no one. Beat: catharsis through fire.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Measured
chapters.summary: Dawn: Hollowmere stands as an ordinary ruin, correctly measured. Wren fades in Marguerite's arms, thanking them for finishing the game. Marguerite files a report no one will believe—and a memorial the town must read aloud. Beat: grief with purpose.

chapters.title: The Verse Carried Out
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Marguerite's POV. Months later, they teach the full song to the town's children—not to summon, but to remember. On their porch at dusk, nothing waits, and that absence feels like a door counted correctly. Beat: belonging earned, not haunted.
